title: Adjectives: agreement and nationality
goal: Make an adjective agree with its noun and name a nationality.
theory: An adjective agrees with its noun in gender and number and usually comes after it: `un coche pequeño`, `una casa pequeña`, `unos coches pequeños`. Adjectives ending in `-e` or a consonant do not change for gender: `un chico inteligente`, `una chica inteligente`. Nationalities ending in a consonant add `-a` for the feminine: `español → española`, `alemán → alemana`. Before a masculine singular noun `bueno` and `malo` are shortened: `un buen amigo`, `un mal día`.

title: Comparison and the superlative
goal: Compare two things and pick the best of many.
theory: To compare use `más… que`, `menos… que`, `tan… como`: `Madrid es más grande que Valencia.` `Ana es tan alta como Luis.` With nouns: `tanto/a/os/as… como`: `Tengo tantos libros como tú.` Special forms: `bueno → mejor`, `malo → peor`, `grande → mayor` (older), `pequeño → menor` (younger). The superlative is the article + `más/menos`: `la más alta`, `el menos caro`; after it comes `de`: `la más alta de la clase.`

title: Indefinite words: algo, nada, mucho, poco
goal: Say "someone", "nothing", "a lot", "little" and build the negative correctly.
theory: `Alguien` is someone, `nadie` is no one, `algo` is something, `nada` is nothing: `¿Hay alguien en casa? — No, no hay nadie.` If the negative word comes after the verb, `no` must come before it: `No veo a nadie.` Quantity: `mucho`, `poco`, `bastante`, `demasiado` agree with the noun: `mucha gente`, `pocos amigos`. Without a noun these words do not change: `Trabajo mucho.` `Alguno` and `ninguno` agree, and before a masculine noun they are shortened: `algún día`, `ningún problema`.

title: Object pronouns: lo, la, le
goal: Replace the direct and indirect object with a pronoun.
theory: The direct object (whom, what) is replaced by `me`, `te`, `lo/la`, `nos`, `os`, `los/las`: `Veo a Ana → La veo.` `Compro el libro → Lo compro.` The indirect object (to whom) is `me`, `te`, `le`, `nos`, `os`, `les`: `Doy el libro a Ana → Le doy el libro.` The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb: `Lo tengo.` `No lo tengo.` With an infinitive or gerund it can be attached to the end: `Quiero verla.`

title: Reflexive verbs: me levanto, se llama
goal: Conjugate reflexive verbs and talk about a daily routine.
theory: Reflexive verbs act on the speaker and are conjugated with a pronoun: `me`, `te`, `se`, `nos`, `os`, `se`. `Levantarse`: `me levanto`, `te levantas`, `se levanta`, `nos levantamos`, `os levantáis`, `se levantan`. The pronoun goes before the verb: `Me ducho por la mañana.` Compare: `Lavo el coche` (I wash the car) and `Me lavo` (I wash myself). Many verbs change meaning: `ir` and `irse`, `dormir` and `dormirse`. With an infinitive the pronoun joins it: `Voy a ducharme.`

title: Ser and estar: how they differ
goal: Choose between ser and estar in typical situations.
theory: `Ser` is what something is, `estar` is a state and a place. `Ser` gives qualities, job, origin, time: `Ana es simpática.` `Soy de Madrid.` `Son las tres.` `Estar` gives place and a temporary state: `Ana está cansada.` `Estamos en Madrid.` The same adjective can change meaning: `Es aburrido` — he is a boring person, `Está aburrido` — he is bored now; `Es listo` — clever, `Está listo` — ready. For an event use `ser`: `La fiesta es en mi casa.`

title: Near future: voy a + infinitive
goal: Talk about plans and intentions with ir a.
theory: To talk about plans use `ir a` + infinitive: `Voy a estudiar español.` `Vamos a salir.` Only `ir` is conjugated: `voy a`, `vas a`, `va a`, `vamos a`, `vais a`, `van a`. You can say when with `mañana`, `esta noche`, `el sábado`, `la semana que viene`. For the near future you can also use the present: `Mañana voy al médico.` For a question: `¿Qué vas a hacer?`

title: Estar + gerund: what I am doing now
goal: Say what is happening right now and tell it from a habit.
theory: An action happening at the moment of speaking is expressed with `estar` + gerund: `Estoy estudiando.` `Están comiendo.` Form the gerund like this: `-ar → -ando`, `-er/-ir → -iendo`: `hablar → hablando`, `comer → comiendo`, `vivir → viviendo`. Special forms: `leer → leyendo`, `dormir → durmiendo`, `pedir → pidiendo`. The simple present speaks about a habit: `Estudio por las tardes.` Compare: `Hago deporte` (usually) and `Estoy haciendo deporte` (right now).

title: Pretérito indefinido: what happened
goal: Tell about a completed event in the past.
theory: `Pretérito indefinido` describes a completed action in the past: `Ayer trabajé mucho.` Endings for `-ar`: `-é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron`; for `-er/-ir`: `-í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron`: `hablé`, `comí`, `viví`. Common irregular forms: `ser/ir`: `fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron`; `hacer`: `hice`, `hizo`; `tener`: `tuve`; `estar`: `estuve`. Time markers: `ayer`, `anoche`, `el año pasado`, `hace dos días`.

title: Pretérito perfecto: I have already done it
goal: Talk about an event connected with the present and about life experience.
theory: This is a compound tense: `haber` + past participle. `He`, `has`, `ha`, `hemos`, `habéis`, `han` + `-ado` (`-ar`) or `-ido` (`-er/-ir`): `he trabajado`, `has comido`. Irregular participles: `hecho`, `dicho`, `visto`, `escrito`, `puesto`, `vuelto`, `abierto`. It is used when the period is not over yet: `hoy`, `esta semana`, `este año`, and for experience: `¿Has estado en España?` Markers: `ya`, `todavía no`, `alguna vez`, `nunca`. Nothing goes between `haber` and the participle: `No he comido`.

title: Pretérito imperfecto: how it used to be
goal: Describe habits and the setting in the past.
theory: `Pretérito imperfecto` tells how things used to be and describes the setting. Endings for `-ar`: `-aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban`; for `-er/-ir`: `-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían`: `trabajaba`, `comía`, `vivía`. Only three verbs are irregular: `ser` (`era`), `ir` (`iba`), `ver` (`veía`). Habit markers: `siempre`, `a menudo`, `todos los días`, `cuando era niño`: `Cuando era niña, vivía en un pueblo.`

title: The imperative
goal: Give advice, make requests and prohibit with the imperative.
theory: The affirmative form for `tú` is the third person singular: `habla`, `come`, `escribe`. For `usted`: `hable`, `coma`, `escriba`. The negative for `tú` comes from the subjunctive: `no hables`, `no comas`. Irregular forms for `tú`: `di`, `haz`, `ve`, `pon`, `sal`, `sé`, `ten`, `ven`. Reflexive verbs attach the pronoun to the end: `lávate`, and in the negative it goes before the verb: `no te laves`.

title: Prepositions of place and time: a, en, de, desde
goal: Choose a preposition for direction, place and time.
theory: `A` shows direction and time: `Voy a Madrid.` `Llego a las cinco.` `En` is place and means of transport: `Vivo en Madrid.` `Voy en autobús.` `De` is origin, possession, material: `Soy de Rusia.` `El libro de Ana.` For periods use `desde` (from when) and `hasta` (until when): `Trabajo desde las nueve hasta las cinco.` `Por la mañana` is in the morning. Places: `encima de`, `debajo de`, `al lado de`, `delante de`, `detrás de`, `dentro de`.

title: City and transport
goal: Ask for directions and name a place in town and a means of transport.
theory: City words are needed to ask the way: `¿Dónde está el banco?` Answers: `Todo recto`, `a la derecha`, `a la izquierda`. Transport: `el autobús`, `el metro`, `el tren`, `el taxi`. With transport use the preposition `en`: `Voy en metro`, but `a pie`. Places: `la plaza`, `el banco`, `la farmacia`, `la estación`.

title: Home and everyday things
goal: Describe your flat and name things in a home.
theory: When describing a home name the rooms and furniture: `la cocina`, `el salón`, `el dormitorio`, `el baño`. For where things are: `En mi dormitorio hay una cama y un armario.` Do not confuse `casa` (house) and `piso` (a flat in Spain). Common words: `la mesa`, `la silla`, `el sofá`, `la ventana`.

title: Work and study
goal: Say where you work or study and what you do.
theory: To talk about work you need names of jobs and places. Jobs often have a feminine form: `el camarero / la camarera`, `el médico / la médica`. To ask: `¿A qué te dedicas?` To answer: `Soy ingeniero.` `Trabajo en una oficina.` `Estudio en la universidad.`

title: Reading messages and short letters
goal: Understand a short letter or message and find the main points: who, what, when.
theory: In informal letters the greeting is `Hola, Ana:`; the closing is `Un abrazo`, `Besos`, `Hasta pronto`. In formal ones: `Estimado señor:`, `Atentamente`. In the text look for who is writing, what they ask for and for which day. Verbs of invitation and request: `¿Puedes…?`, `¿Quieres venir…?`, `Te escribo para…`.

vocabulary.translation: I am writing to you to…

title: Reading short news and posters
goal: Understand a headline and the main idea of a short article or poster.
theory: In a short article the headline and the first sentence matter. Find who, what, where and when. You will understand some words from context. On posters look for the date and place: `el 12 de mayo, a las 20:00, en el Teatro Real`. Useful words: `entradas` (tickets), `concierto`, `exposición`, `estreno` (premiere).

title: Writing a message and an invitation
goal: Write a short message to a friend: invite them and agree on a place and time.
theory: An invitation has a greeting, a question and details. A model: `Hola, Pablo: ¿Quieres venir al cine el sábado? La película empieza a las 8. Quedamos en la plaza a las 7. Un abrazo.` Use `¿Quieres…?`, `Podemos…`, `Quedamos…`. Do not forget `¿` and `¡` at the start of a question and an exclamation.

title: Listening to station announcements
goal: Pick out the platform number, time and destination in an announcement.
theory: In announcements catch numbers and places: `El tren con destino a Sevilla sale a las 18:15 de la vía 3.` Besides numbers listen for key words: `sale`, `llega`, `vía`, `retraso`. Do not try to understand everything. Write down the time, the number and the city, then check yourself.

title: Listening to a conversation about plans
goal: Understand what plans two people are talking about and when they will meet.
theory: A conversation about plans is built from questions and answers: `¿Qué vas a hacer?`, `Voy a…`, `¿Quedamos?`. Listen for the time (`mañana`, `el sábado`), the place and agreement or refusal. In lively speech words get shortened: `pa` for `para`, `¿qué tal?` for `¿cómo estás?`. Listen twice.

vocabulary.translation: What are you going to do?

title: Speaking: how to get there
goal: Ask the way and explain how to get somewhere.
theory: To ask the way start politely: `Perdone, ¿dónde está la farmacia?` When you explain, use short phrases: `Siga todo recto.` `Gire a la derecha.` `Está al lado del banco.` Repeat the key words to check you understood: `¿Todo recto y a la izquierda?`

vocabulary.translation: Thank you, you are very kind

title: Speaking: weekend plans
goal: Tell about your plans and suggest meeting.
theory: You talk about plans with `voy a` + infinitive: `Este fin de semana voy a visitar a mis padres.` To suggest: `¿Quieres venir?` `Podemos ir al cine.` To agree: `Vale`, `Me parece bien`. A polite refusal: `Lo siento, no puedo.` Say whole phrases aloud.

vocabulary.translation: We could go to the cinema
